parts.ask: \(y = \sin x\), with \(x\) in radians. Use differentiation from first principles to show that \(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \cos x\). You may use the formula for \(\sin(A \pm B)\), and assume that as \(h \to 0\), \(\dfrac{\sin h}{h} \to 1\) and \(\dfrac{\cos h - 1}{h} \to 0\).

steps.why: The gradient of the chord from \(x\) to \(x + h\), as \(h \to 0\).

steps.tex: \frac{\sin(x + h) - \sin x}{h} = \frac{\sin x\cos h + \cos x\sin h - \sin x}{h}
steps.why: Expand with \(\sin(A + B) = \sin A\cos B + \cos A\sin B\).
Group the terms so both given limits appear.
